data.source_title: Effects of a Dedicated Regional Psychiatric Emergency Service on Boarding of Psychiatric Patients in Area Emergency Departments
data.locator: Abstract; Methods and Results. Boarding measured from patient stable for psychiatric disposition to ED departure for transfer to the regional psychiatric emergency service (PES).
data.source_setting: Five community hospital EDs in Alameda County, California, operating under a regional psychiatric emergency service model for patients on involuntary mental-health holds.
data.source_n: 144 ED patients tracked across five hospitals.
data.quantity: Mean ED boarding time to transfer to regional PES
data.source_evidence_basis: Prospective operational tracking at five EDs. The full open-access original article defines the endpoint from psychiatric disposition stability to ED departure for PES transfer; reported mean was 107.56 minutes.
data.limitations: One county system and a 30-day cohort; regional PES availability and involuntary-hold workflow may not transfer to other settings. Mean is not a distribution, and comparison with older published benchmarks is not a controlled concurrent comparison. Not local RWJ data.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Model psychiatric disposition as assessment/stabilization followed by a dedicated PES transfer option. Use the measured mean only as an external point reference; do not infer a distribution or RWJ-specific wait.

data.source_title: Effects of a Dedicated Regional Psychiatric Emergency Service on Boarding of Psychiatric Patients in Area Emergency Departments
data.locator: Results; Table 2. Disposition after assessment and treatment in regional psychiatric emergency service.
data.source_setting: Same five Alameda County community EDs and regional PES; patients on involuntary mental-health holds.
data.source_n: 144 patients tracked at PES; article reports 37 admitted and 107 discharged.
data.quantity: Disposition after PES evaluation: inpatient psychiatric admission vs discharge
data.unit: percent of patients tracked at PES
data.source_evidence_basis: The full text explicitly reports 24.8% admitted and 75.2% discharged, and separately reports counts 37/144 and 107/144. These percentage and count statements conflict arithmetically: the reported counts imply 25.7% and 74.3%. The record preserves the published percentages and surfaces the discrepancy rather than silently recomputing them.
data.limitations: The article contains an internal percentage/count inconsistency: 37/144 and 107/144 do not equal its stated 24.8% and 75.2%. Resolve against author/source erratum before quantitative use. Single regional service and brief observation window; PES discharge does not establish outpatient follow-up or clinical outcome. Not RWJ data.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent assessment/treatment as a disposition branch between inpatient placement and PES discharge, but exclude the conflicting numeric percentages from calibration until the discrepancy is resolved; calibrate branch rates from local audited outcomes.
